design: BreakGlassGrant: grant_id, requester, reason, incident_ref, scope, domain, capabilities (frozenset), approvers (sorted pair), granted_at, ttl; structural validation in __post_init__ (ValueError), no authority by itself.

BreakGlassController(identities: PrincipalDirectory, stop, clock: TrustedClock, audit: BreakGlassAuditSink, alerts: BreakGlassAlertSink); PrincipalDirectory is the read-only get() surface that IdentityRegistry already provides.

grant(): trusted now -> under lock: mandatory fields, grant-id reuse, forbidden capabilities, principals (requester, approvers, quorum) -> BreakGlassGrant -> audit GRANTED -> alert (failure: audit GRANT_WITHDRAWN, refuse) -> register. Every refusal audited as GRANT_DENIED with its reason code.

authorize(): trusted now -> under lock: issued and unaltered -> revoked -> expiry (auto-revoke) -> not yet valid -> forbidden -> named -> emergency stop -> review reference -> principals re-validated -> audit USE_AUTHORIZED -> alert (failure: audit USE_WITHDRAWN, refuse) -> BreakGlassUse. Every refusal audited as USE_DENIED with its reason code.
revoke(): issued check -> revocation recorded -> audit REVOKED (failure raises, revocation holds).

backend_under_test.break_glass: BreakGlassController is a pure in-memory C6 component (like the sealed OCOR-DEV-0044 slice): its boundary ports are the identity registry (the real c2_identity.IdentityRegistry, plus a mutable read-only directory to model authoritative record changes between grant and use), the trusted clock (kernel.governance.InMemoryTrustedClock, or a settable clock to model a rewound or naive instant), and the synchronous audit and alert sinks (recording doubles that can be made to fail). No external service is involved; no external boundary is mocked.

findings_scope.audit_and_alert: added: grants, uses, refusals, revocations and automatic expiry revocations are appended synchronously to an injected audit sink; grants and uses raise an immediate alert on an injected alert sink; an audit failure fails the operation closed (BREAK_GLASS_AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE), an alert failure withdraws the grant or use with a WITHDRAWN audit event (BREAK_GLASS_ALERT_UNAVAILABLE)
findings_scope.named_capabilities: fixed (X1): the grant carries a non-empty set of named capabilities; forbidden capabilities are refused at grant and at use; authorize refuses any capability not named in the grant (BREAK_GLASS_CAPABILITY_NOT_GRANTED)
findings_scope.point_1_issued_grants_only: fixed: BreakGlassController registers every grant it issues; authorize and revoke honour only a grant equal to the registered one (BREAK_GLASS_GRANT_NOT_ISSUED for a hand-built grant, a grant of another controller or one altered after issuance in capabilities, ttl, granted_at, scope, domain or requester)
findings_scope.point_2_principals_revalidated: fixed: at grant time and at every use the requester must be a resolved ACTIVE principal and never an approver; the two approvers must be distinct, resolved, principal_kind HUMAN, status ACTIVE, and jointly hold SECURITY_DUTY_OFFICER and DOMAIN_OWNER:<grant domain> on distinct approvers; attributes are read only from the registry record; absent or malformed principal_kind/roles fail closed (BREAK_GLASS_PRINCIPAL_ATTRIBUTES_INVALID), status absent or not ACTIVE is inactive
findings_scope.point_3_trusted_time: fixed: the controller takes a kernel.governance.TrustedClock; grant and authorize accept no instant parameter (TypeError on at=); a naive trusted instant fails closed (TemporalGuardViolation); an instant before issuance is refused (BREAK_GLASS_NOT_YET_VALID)
findings_scope.point_4_ttl_no_renewal: already satisfied, kept and re-proved: TTL in (0, 15 min], a grant id is never reissued (BREAK_GLASS_GRANT_ID_REUSED), the public surface is grant/authorize/revoke only
findings_scope.point_5_revocation_and_expiry: re-proved with trusted time and issued grants: revoked or expired grants deny with BREAK_GLASS_EXPIRED; expiry revokes for good (a rewound clock never revives the grant); a revocation holds even when its audit append fails
findings_scope.q1_po_condition: the controller has no write path to the registry and grant takes no attribute, role or kind parameter (TypeError); role tokens placed in reason/scope/incident text are ignored; a requester or approver cannot update its own immutable registry record (IdentityConflictError) and the grant stays refused. GateSignature.role belongs to the Human Gate (REM-0028) and is not part of break-glass. The registry's lack of writer authority for new records is the open decision request REM-0024-IDENTITY-REGISTRY-WRITER-AUTHORITY (draft PR #262), not closed here
findings_scope.unchanged: EmergencyStopController (request_reset class finding is REM-0028), OutcomeReconciler, c2_identity.py, human_gate.py, every other 0044 test, the 0047 tests and code

normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 section 5.4 break-glass quorum 'Security Duty Officer + affected Domain Owner' and 'Requester non approva': SECURITY_DUTY_OFFICER and DOMAIN_OWNER:<grant domain> held by the two distinct approvers (one approver holding both roles covers only one), requester never among them; the grant carries the affected domain explicitly (PO Q1).
ADD v1.3 section 5.5 'Delegation eccezionale firmata': satisfied as 'registered by the controller' per PO point 1 ('firmati o registrati dal controller'); no signature scheme introduced.

LLD v1.1 section 1.1: effective principal and authority attributes are derived from authoritative identity, never accepted from client input: principal attributes only from the registry record (PO Q1 condition).

Principal attribute convention (PO Q1 option 1) is a PoC interpretation on identity-record v1.2 scalar attributes, not a contract extension: principal_kind HUMAN|WORKLOAD, status ACTIVE (anything else or absent = inactive), roles = sorted, unique, single-space separated tokens.
Requester: any resolved ACTIVE principal (human or workload) may request; only humans approve. Fail-closed reading: an unresolved or inactive requester is refused.
Alert scope: grants and uses are alerted (ADD 5.5 'alert immediato'); refusals and revocations are audited only.

requirement_results.command: a grant built outside grant() (unregistered or well-formed approvers), a grant of another controller, an issued grant altered in capabilities/ttl/granted_at/scope/domain/requester, and revoking a never-issued grant: BREAK_GLASS_GRANT_NOT_ISSUED; the unaltered issued grant still authorizes (RED probe on 19ef2a2: forged grant AUTHORIZED)

requester resolved ACTIVE and never an approver; exactly two distinct approvers, resolved, principal_kind HUMAN, status ACTIVE; absent or malformed principal_kind/roles fail closed; an active workload may request but never approve (RED probe on 19ef2a2: workload approver AUTHORIZED, no requester parameter)

SECURITY_DUTY_OFFICER and DOMAIN_OWNER:<grant domain> on two distinct approvers in either order are accepted; two officers, an owner of another domain, no officer, or one approver holding both roles beside an approver holding neither: BREAK_GLASS_ROLE_QUORUM_UNMET

attribute, role or kind parameters in the grant request are rejected (TypeError); role tokens in reason/scope/incident text are ignored; a requester or approver cannot update its own immutable registry record (IdentityConflictError) and the grant stays refused; grant/authorize/revoke never write the registry

after a successful first use, an approver removed, suspended, turned workload, stripped of its owner role or given malformed roles, or a requester disabled or removed in the authoritative directory makes the next use fail with the matching reason code; unchanged principals keep authorizing while unrelated records change

grant and authorize take no instant (TypeError on at=); granted_at and every use come from the injected trusted clock; the window closes exactly at expiry; an instant before issuance is BREAK_GLASS_NOT_YET_VALID; a naive trusted instant fails closed (RED probe on 19ef2a2: back-dated and future-dated caller instants AUTHORIZED)

TTL in (0, 15 min] with the bound accepted and 0, negative or 15 min + 1 s refused and audited; a grant id is never reissued and the public surface is grant/authorize/revoke; expiry revokes for good even if the trusted clock is rewound; revocation denies immediately, is audited, and holds when its audit append fails

a grant needs named capabilities, reason, incident, scope and domain; none of the eight forbidden capabilities can be named or used; a named capability authorizes, an unnamed one is BREAK_GLASS_CAPABILITY_NOT_GRANTED; an active emergency stop and a missing review reference still refuse (RED probe on 19ef2a2: capability outside the scope AUTHORIZED)

grants and uses are audited before they take effect and alerted immediately; an audit failure refuses the grant or use (BREAK_GLASS_AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE), an alert failure withdraws it with a WITHDRAWN audit event (BREAK_GLASS_ALERT_UNAVAILABLE) and the grant is never registered; refused grants and uses are audited with their reason code and stay refused when the audit fails

residual_risks: Writer authority of IdentityRegistry for new records (a first writer can register a new principal with self-declared privileged attributes): open decision request REM-0024-IDENTITY-REGISTRY-WRITER-AUTHORITY (draft PR #262), required before G6; this remediation reads the registry only and does not close it.

The concrete IdentityRegistry is immutable per record, so deactivation or role removal between grant and use is exercised with a mutable read-only directory implementing the same get() surface; no lifecycle API for principal records exists yet.

Audit and alert sinks are ports: durability and immutability of a production audit store and delivery of the alert are properties of the injected implementations, not of this component; G6 qualification (FR-108, FR-134, FR-139, FR-146, NFR-081) must bind them to real backends.
Post-review is structural (mandatory review reference on every use) but no review workflow exists; LLD 'review obbligatoria' completion is outside this remediation.
Emergency-stop reset (request_reset: existence-only approvers, caller instant) and the Human Gate (GateSignature.role, caller instants) remain as found: OCOR-DEV-REM-0028, after this remediation.
BreakGlassController is not yet wired into a live PoC path (in_live_poc_path false in the registration); runtime conformance is NOT_ESTABLISHED.
